trust_decision.summary: Whether an UNTRUSTED (Docker HTTP body) config may supply a caller-chosen regular expression to the server; decided in the untrusted deserialization gate (_filter_untrusted_fields / _clamp_untrusted, called from from_serializable_dict) in crawl4ai/async_configs.py.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'ReDoS via /crawl Regex Fields'; the schema field 'regex' step that runs re.search with a caller pattern is the obvious sink. The published fix is not there but in the gate in crawl4ai/async_configs.py.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /crawl, /crawl/stream, /crawl/job (deploy/docker/server.py:955, deploy/docker/server.py:1006, deploy/docker/api.py:997) -> CrawlerRunConfig.load(provenance=UNTRUSTED) (deploy/docker/api.py:689, deploy/docker/api.py:912) -> forbidden-field map for RegexExtractionStrategy.custom and RegexChunking.patterns
fix_sites.module_kind: config deserialization / trust gate (core library, not the Docker server)

fix_sites.entry_point: same HTTP routes -> _clamp_untrusted schema walk for JsonCss/JsonXPath/JsonLxmlExtractionStrategy

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: crawl4ai/async_configs.py:550-564 (the {"type":"dict","value":...} envelope, which the fix's walk must see through, fix.diff:113-114); also RegexChunking.patterns sink at crawl4ai/chunking_strategy.py:56-59, a chunking feature next door to the extraction feature the report names

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names 'regex fields' in the extraction schema, so RegexChunking (a chunking strategy) and RegexExtractionStrategy.custom look like neighbouring features. A list-valued 'type' pipeline (['text','regex']) looks like a different field type from 'regex', so a type == 'regex' check feels complete.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Untrusted callers must keep the built-in RegexExtractionStrategy patterns (pattern=<IntFlag>), JsonCss/XPath/Lxml schemas without regex fields (including non-regex list pipelines like ['attribute']), and trusted/SDK use of custom regexes and RegexChunking.patterns must stay unchanged. Banning RegexExtractionStrategy or Json* schemas outright, or gating regardless of provenance, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: RegexExtractionStrategy.custom as a list of (label, regex) pairs (crawl4ai/extraction_strategy.py:2703-2704; the field-name ban covers both)
schema field with type 'regex' at top level (fix.diff:110)
regex field nested inside a 'nested' field (fix.diff:112)
three schema strategies: JsonCss, JsonXPath, JsonLxml (fix.diff:37-39, fix.diff:119)

O7_producer.where: crawl4ai/extraction_strategy.py:1203-1205 (the field-schema interpreter turns 'type' into a step pipeline, so a list containing 'regex' runs re.search at crawl4ai/extraction_strategy.py:1214-1221)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A schema field whose 'type' is a list pipeline containing 'regex' (e.g. ['text','regex'] with 'pattern') reaches re.search, but the published walk only matches type == 'regex', so it is not refused.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The pipeline form is a newer feature (tests/test_pr_1290_1668.py:55-84) and is not mentioned in the report; a solver checking 'type == "regex"' and verifying with the report's example would call it fully covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Other file from the gate (crawl4ai/async_configs.py), same package; the differential sits in how the schema interpreter normalises 'type', which the gate never calls.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: LinkPreviewConfig include_patterns/exclude_patterns compiled with re instead of fnmatch (an allowed untrusted type with no field allowlist)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Users ask for regex URL filters; a maintainer swapping fnmatch for re.search to support them would open the same sink through a type the gate allows.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CrawlerRunConfig.url_matcher gaining a 're:' prefix mode (url_matcher is on the untrusted allowlist at crawl4ai/async_configs.py:295)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: match helpers commonly add a regex mode next to glob; it would sit in the allowlist with no new type.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: negative_patterns exposed as a constructor argument on PruningContentFilter/BM25ContentFilter (both untrusted-allowed types)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The hard-coded noise regex is an obvious tuning knob to expose; a maintainer would add it as a ctor arg with no thought for the gate.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333): caller-controlled regular expression reaching Python re on server-side page content, missing untrusted-input gate

O10_build.toolchain: pip install -e . (pyproject.toml); pytest. The gate tests need no browser (tests/unit/test_untrusted_field_sinks.py:9).
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/test_untrusted_field_sinks.py (gate tests via CrawlerRunConfig.load with Provenance.UNTRUSTED); deploy/docker/tests/test_security_trust_boundary.py; tests/test_pr_1290_1668.py (schema pipeline/regex extraction behaviour)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Refuse schema fields with type == 'regex' (or remove the regex step / add a timeout in extraction_strategy.py) and stop. That misses RegexExtractionStrategy.custom, RegexChunking.patterns and the list-pipeline type, or it breaks trusted SDK users.

out_of_scope_notes: LinkPreviewConfig include/exclude_patterns use fnmatch (crawl4ai/link_preview.py:142, crawl4ai/link_preview.py:152); CPython >=3.9 fnmatch.translate avoids '*' backtracking, so this was not counted as a route.
